 Near Kishan Dharam Kanta,
 Ghaziabad, UP.

 2) Manoj  S/o Nepal Singh  R/o H. No. 15, Loni Road, Bhopura  in front of New Petrol Pump,
 Ghaziabad, UP.
Offence complained of : U/s 170/171/419/420/34 IPC Plea of accused : Pleaded not guilty Date of institution: 23.02.2016 Date of reserving the order: 03.11.2025 Date of order : 07.11.2025 FIR No. 235/2012 Page No. 1 of 4  Final order : ACQUITTAL  JUDGMENT State vs Mangal@Sanjay on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91010092/
1

BRIEF REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE:-
1.

Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution is that on 04.07.2012 at about 3.15PM at B.B.M. Depot, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Mukherji Nagar, both the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention, cheated complainant Sh. Mohan Singh by impersonating themselves as public servant/officials of police by wearing police uniform and dishonestly induced the complainant to deliver them Rs. 6000/-.

It thereby alleged that the accused have committed offences punishable u/s 170/171/419/420/34 IPC.
2.
Upon completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 173 Cr.PC was filed by the IO for offences punishable u/s 419/420/34 IPC.
The cognizance of offence was taken and copy of charge sheet was supplied to the accused.
After compliance of provisions U/s 207 Cr.P.C., the charge was framed against the accused Manoj for the offences U/s 170/171/419/420/34 IPC on 05.05.2025.
The accused Mangal @ Sanjay failed to appear in the court despite issuance of all coercive processes.

He was declared as absconder vide order dated 14.10.2024.
3.
Matter was then listed for PE.

Prosecution listed as many as 09 witnesses of which only complainant Sh. Mohan Singh is a witness to the offence, whose testimony was essential to identify the accused persons and establish the commission of offence.
However, summons issued to the complainant received back with the report that he has already expired on 28.01.2016.

Accordingly,
the said witness was dropped from the list of prosecution witnesses vide order dated 03.11.2025.
4.
All remaining prosecution witnesses cited were formal witnesses and were only to depose in regards to the investigation undertaken in the present FIR.

Thus, they were not examined and vide order dated 03.11.2025, prosecution evidence was closed since there was no other material prosecution witness who could have connected the accused persons with the offence in question.

6. Further, since no material incriminating evidence against the accused persons was brought on record by the prosecution, recording of statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.P.C. was dispensed with and matter was fixed for hearing of final arguments on the same date.
7. I have heard Ld. APP for the State and also perused the evidence on record.

8. While the prosecution has alleged that the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention cheated complainant Sh. Mohan Singh by impersonating themselves as public servant/officials of police by wearing police uniform and dishonestly induced the complainant to deliver them Rs. 6000/- however, the complainant who was the victim in the present case was never brought before this court for deposing on oath.
Further no independent witness or evidence was brought on record to establish the offences and identity of the accused persons.

In such circumstances, it cannot be said that the prosecution has State vs Mangal@Sanjay on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91010092/
2 successfully proven the ingredients of the offences punishable u/s 170/171/419/420/34 IPC.
9.

In view of the failure of the prosecution to establish its case beyond doubt, accused Manoj S/o Nepal Singh is acquitted for the offences punishable U/s 506/509(1)/427/34 IPC.
10.
File be consigned to Record Room to be revived as and when any fresh leads about the accused Mangal @ Sanjay S/o Anand are found.
